q: Electrolysis is the process whereby ____ is used to bring about a chemical change.
e: Electrolysis is the process whereby electrical energy is used to bring about a chemical change. Electrolysis uses electrical energy to force a non-spontaneous chemical change.

q: In a ____, electric current can flow freely, but in a non-conductor (an insulator) it cannot.
e: In a conductor, electric current can flow freely, but in a non-conductor (an insulator) it cannot. An insulator, or non-conductor, does not let electric current flow freely.

q: All metals either in the ____ or liquid state are conductors.
e: All metals either in the solid state or liquid state are conductors. Metals either in the or liquid state are.

q: Solid substances such as wood, plastic and rubber do not conduct electricity and they are ____.
e: Solid substances such as wood, plastic and rubber do not conduct electricity and they are non-conductors or insulators. Wood, plastic and rubber are insulators. they do not provide mobile electrons or ions. An insulator, or non-conductor, does not let electric current flow freely.

q: ____ are substances which have an ability to conduct between conductors and non-conductors.
e: Semiconductors are substances which have an ability to conduct between conductors and non-conductors. A semiconductor conducts between a metal and an insulator. silicon and germanium are the usual examples.

q: Electrolytes are substances that ____ in solution or in a molten state and can conduct electricity.
e: Electrolytes are substances that ionise in solution or in a molten state and can conduct electricity. Metals conduct in the solid or molten state because they have mobile electrons. An electrolyte ionises in solution or in the molten state so the ions can carry current. Ionisation in solution or in the melt produces mobile ions that can carry current.

q: Most electrolytes are ____ such as salt solutions.
e: Most electrolytes are ionic compounds such as salt solutions. An electrolyte ionises in solution or in the molten state so the ions can carry current.

q: Acid and base solutions are also electrolytes: strong acid and strong base solutions are ____, weak acid and weak base solutions are weak electrolytes.
e: Acid and base solutions are also electrolytes: strong acid and strong base solutions are strong electrolytes, weak acid and weak base solutions are weak electrolytes. An electrolyte ionises in solution or in the molten state so the ions can carry current.

q: Non-electrolytes do not ____ in solution and cannot conduct electricity.
e: Non-electrolytes do not dissociate into ions in solution and cannot conduct electricity. An electrolyte ionises in solution or in the molten state so the ions can carry current.

e: They are covalent compounds such as sugar solution. A covalent bond is a shared pair of electrons between atoms.

q: Electrodes are usually made of unreactive metals such as ____ or non-metal carbon(graphite) through which the electric current enters and leaves the electrolyte.
e: Electrodes are usually made of unreactive metals such as platinum or non-metal carbon(graphite) through which the electric current enters and leaves the electrolyte. Electrodes are often platinum or graphite so the electrode itself does not react. An electrolyte ionises in solution or in the molten state so the ions can carry current. Electrodes are the conductors where oxidation and reduction happen during electrolysis.

q: ____ reactions take place at the electrodes.
e: Reduction and oxidation reactions take place at the electrodes. Electrodes are the conductors where oxidation and reduction happen during electrolysis.

q: Cathode attracts the ____.
e: Cathode attracts the positively charged ions (cations). The cathode is the electrode where reduction occurs.

q: Anode attracts ____.
e: Anode attracts negatively charged ions (anions). The anode is the electrode where oxidation occurs.

q: Thus, the reduction reaction takes place at the ____ and the oxidation reaction takes place at the anode.
e: Thus, the reduction reaction takes place at the cathode and the oxidation reaction takes place at the anode. The anode is the electrode where oxidation occurs.

q: An electrochemical cell is a device that converts ____ or vice versa when a chemical reaction occurs by electrical energy.
e: An electrochemical cell is a device that converts chemical energy into electrical energy or vice versa when a chemical reaction occurs by electrical energy. An electrochemical cell converts chemical energy to electrical energy, or the reverse in electrolysis.

q: There are two fundamental types of electrochemical cells: ____.
e: There are two fundamental types of electrochemical cells: electrolytic cell and chemical cell. An electrochemical cell converts chemical energy to electrical energy, or the reverse in electrolysis.
